verification.sourceNote: ClaimDesk generic guidance on hidden-damage checks after a collision, compiled from general UK body-repair practice. Not a manufacturer repair method. Recommendations only: the engineer decides which checks are carried out and follows the manufacturer procedure.

rules.label: Structural measurement (jig / 3D measuring system)
rules.reason: Damage is recorded on a structural member; the body should be measured against the manufacturer dimensions before and after repair to confirm the shell is straight.

rules.label: Structural measurement (jig / 3D measuring system)
rules.reason: Heavy damage to an outer panel often means load has passed into the structure behind it, which cannot be seen in photos.

rules.label: Structural measurement (jig / 3D measuring system)
rules.reason: A heavy side impact through a door can push in the B-pillar, sill and floor behind it.

rules.label: Structural measurement (jig / 3D measuring system)
rules.reason: The reported speed and the visible damage together suggest enough energy to reach the structure.

rules.label: Structural measurement (jig / 3D measuring system)
rules.reason: An airbag deployment indicates a significant deceleration; the shell should be measured even if the outer damage looks moderate.

rules.label: Structural measurement (jig / 3D measuring system)
rules.reason: Roof or rollover damage can distort the pillars and roof structure, which needs measuring.

rules.label: Four-wheel alignment / geometry check
rules.reason: Damage to a wheel or suspension component can alter the steering and suspension geometry; the alignment should be checked and any bent parts found.

rules.label: Four-wheel alignment / geometry check
rules.reason: An impact to the corner of the vehicle near a wheel often reaches the wheel and suspension even when they look undamaged in photos.

rules.label: Suspension inspection {sideLabel} (arms, struts, hub, bushes)
rules.reason: Wheel strikes commonly bend lower arms, struts and hubs; the suspension on the impact side should be inspected on a ramp.

rules.label: Suspension inspection {sideLabel} (arms, struts, hub, bushes)
rules.reason: Visible damage to a wheel or suspension part means the components behind it may also be bent.

rules.label: Steering inspection (rack, track rods, steering angle sensor)
rules.reason: A front wheel strike can bend the track rods or damage the steering rack; an off-centre steering wheel after the incident is a typical sign.

rules.label: Pre- and post-repair diagnostic scan (all modules)
rules.reason: Modern vehicles store fault and crash codes in many modules; a scan before and after repair shows hidden electrical faults and confirms systems are working.

rules.label: Pre- and post-repair diagnostic scan (all modules)
rules.reason: Medium or heavy damage usually disturbs sensors, lamps or wiring; a full scan before and after repair is needed.

rules.label: Pre- and post-repair diagnostic scan (all modules)
rules.reason: Damage is recorded on an electrical or sensor component, which will log faults that must be read and cleared.

rules.label: ADAS camera / radar calibration check after wheel alignment
rules.reason: Driver-assistance cameras and radars use the vehicle’s thrust line; if the wheel alignment is adjusted the manufacturer may require the systems to be calibrated.

rules.label: Windscreen camera calibration
rules.reason: Systems using the windscreen camera must be calibrated after the screen is replaced, following the manufacturer procedure.

rules.label: Front radar calibration / alignment
rules.reason: Damage or repair in the area of the front radar can change its aim; the radar alignment must be checked and calibrated to the manufacturer procedure.

rules.label: Rear corner radar calibration (blind spot / cross-traffic)
rules.reason: Damage near the rear corners can move the blind-spot radars behind the bumper; they should be checked and calibrated if disturbed.

rules.label: Parking sensor function test
rules.reason: Bumper damage or repair can leave parking sensors misaligned or painted too thickly; their function should be tested after repair.

rules.label: Airbag / SRS system check and crash data clear
rules.reason: Deployment is indicated: the SRS system must be diagnosed, deployed parts identified and the crash data cleared or the control unit replaced to the manufacturer procedure.

rules.label: Airbag / SRS system check and crash data clear
rules.reason: A heavy impact can be recorded by the airbag control unit or trigger pretensioners without visible deployment.

rules.label: Airbag / SRS system check and crash data clear
rules.reason: Side-impact sensors are mounted in the doors and B-pillars; damage there can affect the sensors or their wiring.

rules.label: Seatbelt inspection (webbing, buckles, retractors, pretensioners)
rules.reason: Belts that were worn in a crash with deployment are typically replaced; pretensioners that fired cannot be reused.

rules.label: Seatbelt inspection (webbing, buckles, retractors, pretensioners)
rules.reason: In a heavy impact the belts and retractors are loaded and should be inspected to the manufacturer guidance.

rules.label: Seatbelt inspection (webbing, buckles, retractors, pretensioners)
rules.reason: The reported speed suggests the occupants’ belts may have been loaded.

rules.label: Cooling system pressure test
rules.reason: Damage at the front panel or cooling pack can cause slow coolant leaks that only show under pressure.

rules.label: Cooling system pressure test
rules.reason: A heavy frontal impact usually reaches the radiator behind the front panel.

rules.label: Cooling system pressure test
rules.reason: Fluid is visible on the ground or under the vehicle in the photos; its source should be identified.

rules.label: Air-conditioning pressure / leak test
rules.reason: The air-conditioning condenser sits at the front of the cooling pack and is easily holed; a leak test confirms whether it is intact.

rules.label: Air-conditioning pressure / leak test
rules.reason: A heavy frontal impact commonly damages the condenser or its pipes behind the bumper.

rules.label: High-voltage system safety check (isolation, battery housing, cables)
rules.reason: On an electrified vehicle medium or heavy damage can reach high-voltage cables or the battery; a qualified technician should check isolation before repair.

rules.label: High-voltage system safety check (isolation, battery housing, cables)
rules.reason: The traction battery and high-voltage cables run under the floor and sills; damage in this area needs a high-voltage safety check before the vehicle is moved into the workshop.

rules.label: High-voltage system safety check (isolation, battery housing, cables)
rules.reason: An airbag deployment on an electrified vehicle normally triggers high-voltage disconnection; the system must be checked and reset by a qualified technician.

rules.label: Panel gaps and fit of doors, bonnet and tailgate
rules.reason: Uneven gaps or doors that bind show hidden distortion of the hinge pillars or apertures.

rules.label: Underbody inspection on a ramp
rules.reason: Damage is recorded on or near the underbody, which photos rarely show fully.

rules.label: Underbody inspection on a ramp
rules.reason: Heavy impacts can bend subframes, fuel and brake lines and floor sections that are not visible from above.

rules.label: Underbody inspection on a ramp
rules.reason: Fluid is visible in the photos; the underside should be inspected to find the source.

rules.label: Wheel and tyre inspection {sideLabel} (rim, sidewall)
rules.reason: A corner or side impact at wheel height can crack a rim or damage a tyre sidewall, which is not always visible in photos.

rules.label: Headlamp aim (beam setting)
rules.reason: A replaced or refitted headlamp must be aimed so it meets MOT beam requirements and does not dazzle.

rules.label: Headlamp aim (beam setting)
rules.reason: Work on the front panel, bumper or wings disturbs the headlamp mountings, so the beam aim should be checked.

rules.label: Glass inspection for stress cracks (windscreen, sunroof, side glass)
rules.reason: Distortion of the roof or pillars can put the bonded glass under stress and cause cracks to appear later.

rules.label: Glass inspection for stress cracks (windscreen, sunroof, side glass)
rules.reason: A passenger airbag deployment can strike and crack the windscreen.
